references.text: Laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal is a central part of the sacrifice rituals, where sin is symbolically transferred to the animal.
The same ritual with laying on of hands and slaughter of the bull before the Lord is described for the priest's sin offering.
Aaron places both hands on the goat's head and confesses Israel's sins, demonstrating the significance of laying on of hands for the transfer of sin.
At the consecration of the priests, Aaron and his sons were to lay their hands on the bull's head before it was slaughtered.
The Israelites laid their hands on the Levites as part of the consecration ritual, showing the representative function of laying on of hands.
Slaughter of the sacrificial animal before the Lord in the same place as the burnt offering confirms the fixed place of sacrifice.
The sacrifices of the Old Testament with bull's blood point forward to Christ's perfect sacrifice that cleanses the conscience.
